audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Graves Level 1 and Level 6 and called Level 2 a skill matchup, but the whys under those very rows describe the opposite: whys[0] calls Level 1 'a genuine standoff', whys[1] says the W block shuts off Graves entirely, and whys[4] says Stand United is free pressure Graves cannot answer.
audit.why: Emerald+ win rate is 36.11% and the packet chart is Shen from Level 2 onward. The prose was already right; only the side tokens were wrong.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Shen / Shen / Shen / Shen / Shen / Shen and the three phase whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as a Graves spike ('Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback'), which reverses who actually spikes.
audit.why: Stand United is 200/180/160s, global, and shields the target ally before the teleport — it wins Shen the map at 6 whether or not he wins the duel. Collateral Damage on 100/80/60s does not threaten a tank who has Ki Barrier shielding him on every cast.
audit.corrected: phases[4] flipped to Shen and its why rewritten around Stand United.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Spirit's Refuge as blanking Graves' whole kit — 'W can negate the burst', 'your Eclipse spike does nothing through a block'. Riot's text blocks attacks only, not abilities.
audit.why: Shen W: 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked.' End of the Line and Collateral Damage are abilities and pass straight through the zone. That is the difference between having no play into an active W and having a real one.
audit.corrected: Stated explicitly in early, spikes[0], whys[2] and whys[5]: autos are eaten, Q and R are not.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shadow Dash was named as the matchup-defining cooldown on six different fields and never numbered once.
audit.why: Shadow Dash is 600 range, 18/16/14/12/10s, 150 energy. Twilight Assault is 400 range on 8/7.25/6.5/5.75/5s and slows enemies running away from him — the reason disengaging after a taunt is not free.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into the cooldown block, dosFull[0], report[5], early and mid.

edits.before: Four shells of buckshot win any level-1 face-off — trade autos point-blank where every pellet lands.
edits.after: Neither of you wants the level-1 trade — no Quickdraw banked for you, only Twilight Assault for him.

edits.before: E online — dash-reload weaving starts: auto, E for the grit armor and reset, auto again. Most champs lose this flat.
edits.after: Spirit's Refuge lands and blocks every attack inside it — your reload-limited shell DPS has no answer to that zone.

edits.before: Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback in one — hold it for either, never for chip.
edits.after: Stand United shields an ally and teleports a screen away — he wins the map while you reload in lane.

edits.before: - Shen Shadow Dash (Taunt): matchup-defining — His taunt engage — punish hard while it is on cooldown. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E dash like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Shen Shadow Dash (Taunt): matchup-defining — a 600-range taunt dash on 10-18s and 150 energy. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E dash like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: His taunt engage — punish hard while it is on cooldown. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: A 600-range taunt dash, 10-18s — punish hard while it is down. Until it's spent, every commit is a coin flip.

edits.before: Track Shen’s Shadow Dash (Taunt): His taunt engage — punish hard while it is on cooldown. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Shen’s Shadow Dash: a 600-range taunt dash, 10-18s — punish hard while it is down. The whole green-light system is that cooldown.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Your W cuts sight range on tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip.

edits.before: Even on your strongest level-3 all-in his E taunt can lock you for its full duration and W can negate the burst, so he edges the one trade you most want.
edits.after: Even on your best level-3 all-in Shadow Dash taunts from 600 and Spirit's Refuge eats your autos — only your Q and R pass through it, so he edges the trade.

edits.before: His first tank item makes the taunt-into-W combo unbeatable for you, while your Eclipse spike does nothing through a block and your armor stacking is irrelevant against his flat damage.
edits.after: His first tank item makes the taunt-into-Refuge combo unbeatable, and your Eclipse spike only reaches him as Q and R — the attack damage it buys is exactly what the zone eats.

edits.before: Shen's W (Spirit's Refuge) puts down a zone that blocks every auto-attack inside it, so your point-blank 4-shell spread and crit burst get eaten the moment you step in to commit a trade.
edits.after: Shen's W (Spirit's Refuge, 10-16s) blocks attacks inside it, so your point-blank 4-shell spread is eaten the moment you commit — but abilities are not blocked, so End of the Line still lands.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — neither of you wants the first trade, since you have no Quickdraw charges to disengage and Shen has only his Q empower online. Your problem starts the second he picks up W (Spirit's Refuge): that zone blocks every auto inside it, so your 4-shell spread and reload-pressured DPS vanish if you commit while it is up. Last-hit with the tip of Q (End of the Line) and never dump autos into the block. Your one real opening is level 3: E in with two Quickdraw charges, drop Smoke Screen on him to slow him and gut his vision, land the Q cone, and Quickdraw back out before his taunt is off cooldown.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — neither of you wants the first trade, since you have no Quickdraw charges to disengage and Shen has only his Q empower online. Your problem starts the second he picks up W (Spirit's Refuge): that zone blocks attacks, so your 4-shell spread vanishes if you commit while it is up — it blocks nothing else, so End of the Line and Collateral Damage still land through it. Last-hit with the tip of Q and never dump autos into the block. Your one real opening is level 3: E in with two Quickdraw charges, drop Smoke Screen to slow him and gut his vision, land the Q cone, and Quickdraw out before Shadow Dash (600 range, 10-18s) is back.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are where Shen pulls ahead, and his E taunt is the whole matchup: if it lands, you are dragged into melee for its full duration while your True Grit armor stacks do nothing against a tank, and his empowered Q (Twilight Assault) out-trades your two-shot magazine through every reload. Bait the taunt or sidestep the dash with Quickdraw before you ever throw your combo. At 6 his R (Stand United) means he does not even have to win lane — he shields an ally and presses an objective the instant you push the wave or step back to reload.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are where Shen pulls ahead, and Shadow Dash is the whole matchup: 600 range on 18/16/14/12/10s, and if it lands you are taunted into melee while your True Grit stacks do nothing against a tank. Twilight Assault hits for max health every 5-8s and slows you while you run away from him, so disengaging after a taunt is not free either. Bait the dash with Quickdraw before you ever throw your combo. At 6 his R (Stand United) means he does not even have to win lane — he shields an ally and presses an objective the instant you push the wave or step back to reload.

notes: The single most useful correction: Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks, not abilities. The page repeatedly implied it blanked Graves' whole kit, which leaves the reader with no play; in fact End of the Line and Collateral Damage pass through the zone, and that is how you keep damage on him while the W is up. Level chart sides contradicted their own explanations in both layers and are now aligned to the packet chart and the 36% win rate.
